articles.title: Magnésio: por que esse mineral ganhou tanto espaço na suplementação? | G1
articles.standfirst: Entenda as funções do mineral no organismo, sua relação com a atividade física e o papel da suplementação na rotina.
articles.summary: Entenda as funções do mineral no organismo, sua relação com a atividade física e o papel da suplementação na rotina.
articles.body:
O magnésio está presente em diversos alimentos e participa de funções importantes do organismo. Ele atua como cofator em centenas de reações bioquímicas, relacionadas ao metabolismo energético, à síntese de proteínas, ao funcionamento muscular e neuromuscular e ao equilíbrio de eletrólitos.

Essa variedade de funções ajuda a explicar por que o mineral passou a aparecer com tanta frequência nas conversas sobre alimentação, atividade física e suplementação. É justamente por estar envolvido em diferentes processos do organismo que o magnésio também ganhou espaço entre os nutrientes presentes em suplementos alimentares.

Na Maltta Nutrition , o magnésio aparece em uma linha diversificada, com diferentes formas do mineral, combinações com outros nutrientes e formatos de apresentação. Entre as opções estão produtos com malato, taurato, quelato e cloreto de magnésio, além de formulações que combinam o mineral com cálcio, vitaminas D3 e K2, cúrcuma ou inositol. Dentro dessa variedade, o 3 Magnésios Inositol se destaca por reunir três formas de magnésio: bisglicinato, óxido e malato com inositol, estando disponível tanto em cápsulas quanto em pó e em diferentes sabores. Assim, a linha oferece diferentes possibilidades para quem busca incluir o magnésio na rotina de suplementação, de acordo com as características e preferências de cada pessoa.

Mas, afinal, o que torna o magnésio tão importante e por que existem diferentes formas desse mineral nos suplementos? Entender suas funções e as características de cada formulação pode ajudar a fazer escolhas mais conscientes na hora de incluir a suplementação na rotina.

Linha 3 Magnésios + Inositol, da Maltta Nutrition. — Foto: Acervo particular Maltta Nutrition + IA ChatGPT.

O magnésio participa de processos fundamentais para o funcionamento normal do organismo. Entre suas funções estão o auxílio no metabolismo energético, no metabolismo de proteínas, carboidratos e gorduras, no equilíbrio dos eletrólitos, no funcionamento muscular e neuromuscular e na formação de ossos e dentes.

Na prática, isso significa que não estamos falando de um nutriente associado a uma única função. Ele está envolvido em diferentes processos que acontecem continuamente no organismo.

Por reunir tantas funções, o magnésio pode ser especialmente relevante para quem mantém uma rotina ativa, já que o funcionamento adequado dos músculos e o metabolismo energético fazem parte do dia a dia de quem pratica exercícios . Manter uma ingestão adequada do mineral, portanto, contribui para o funcionamento normal desses processos.

O magnésio está naturalmente presente em alimentos como verduras verde-escuras, castanhas e outras oleaginosas, sementes e cereais integrais.

Uma alimentação variada pode contribuir para alcançar as necessidades diárias do mineral. No entanto, determinadas situações podem dificultar a ingestão ou aumentar o risco de inadequação. Pessoas com algumas doenças gastrintestinais, adultos mais velhos e indivíduos que utilizam determinados medicamentos, por exemplo, podem apresentar maior risco de inadequação de magnésio. Por isso, é importante realizar acompanhamento profissional.

Por que o magnésio aparece tanto nos suplementos?

Uma das razões está justamente na amplitude de funções que o mineral desempenha. Diferentemente de nutrientes associados principalmente a uma função específica, o magnésio participa de processos relacionados à energia, músculos, proteínas, eletrólitos e estrutura óssea.

Além disso, existem diferentes formas de apresentação do magnésio nos suplementos. A escolha da formulação pode considerar a composição do produto, a quantidade fornecida e o objetivo nutricional.

A Maltta Nutrition, por exemplo, oferece o 3 Magnésios Inositol , que combina bisglicinato, óxido e malato de magnésio com inositol. Cada porção de 7 g fornece 330 mg de magnésio. A combinação de diferentes formas de magnésio em uma mesma formulação é um dos diferenciais do produto, que pode fazer parte de uma rotina de suplementação de forma prática e adequada às necessidades individuais.

Como acontece com qualquer suplemento alimentar, é importante seguir as recomendações de uso presentes na embalagem. O consumo desse suplemento não é recomendado para gestantes, lactantes e crianças.

Magnésio e atividade física: qual é a relação?

O funcionamento muscular é uma das áreas em que o magnésio tem participação reconhecida. O mineral auxilia no funcionamento muscular e neuromuscular e também está envolvido no metabolismo energético.

Por participar do funcionamento muscular e do metabolismo energético, o magnésio também chama a atenção de quem pratica atividades físicas e busca manter uma alimentação nutricionalmente adequada. Nesse contexto, garantir uma ingestão adequada do mineral contribui para que o organismo desempenhe normalmente essas funções.

Magnésio: suplemento ou parte da alimentação?

Uma alimentação variada continua sendo a principal fonte de nutrientes, enquanto o suplemento pode atuar como complemento quando existe necessidade.

O crescimento do interesse pelo magnésio faz sentido diante da quantidade de funções das quais esse mineral participa. Para quem busca complementar a ingestão desse nutriente, a suplementação pode ser uma forma prática de incluí-lo na rotina, especialmente quando alinhada às necessidades individuais. Afinal, cuidar da nutrição não significa simplesmente consumir mais nutrientes, mas oferecer ao organismo aquilo de que ele precisa, na quantidade e no contexto adequados.

articles.title: As Anthropic and OpenAI are set for IPOs, Broadcom CEO has a message for AI investors: For now, it is still losing money

articles.body: With frontier artificial intelligence (AI) labs Anthropic and OpenAI moving toward historic Initial Public Offerings (IPO), Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has issued a blunt warning to AI investors: despite the towering valuations, the generative AI sector remains an unprofitable endeavour. Speaking at an industry gathering in Singapore organised by DBS Bank, the leader of the $1.7 trillion semiconductor supplier framed AI as a volatile and uncertain financial bet at current times.“For now, it’s still losing money,” Tan said of the AI sector, adding, “So frankly, it doesn’t tell anything at this point except that there is a lot of potential revenue growth out of providing frontier generative AI models.”Anthropic is expected to list publicly around Thanksgiving, targeting a valuation in the $2 trillion territory, with OpenAI projected to follow closely behind. Both companies are depending on a vast international build-out of data centres, semiconductor wafers, advanced processor manufacturing and cloud computing capacity to fulfill market demand and eventually turn a profit.Tan warned that a looming shortage of investment capital will likely form the industry's next major roadblock to continued expansion.‘Like they are in a casino’The assessment comes from an executive whose company directly finances its growth by supplying essential hardware components for the AI boom, with Broadcom's equity rising nearly 10% this year. Tan argued that many market participants are pouring money into technologies they fundamentally fail to grasp, comparing enterprise spending behavior to children wasting coins in an arcade.“A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in,” Tan remarked, according to Bloomberg. They “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”“When you are a kid, you go to a video arcade, you play. Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes and you haven’t learned anything. That’s what happening in enterprises today,” he added.Sharing the stage alongside Tan, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan voiced similar caution regarding infrastructure limits. He noted that physical hardware supplies will remain constrained over the next few years, warning that memory chip shortages could become the first segment within the broader AI ecosystem to experience a slowdown.You use AI every day. articles.title: Alibaba Unveils $450 AI Glasses in Expanding Push Into Gadgets
articles.summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. on Tuesday unveiled the new generation of its smart glasses, deepening its foray into consumer electronics as an extension of its...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. on Tuesday unveiled the new generation of its smart glasses, deepening its foray into consumer electronics as an extension of its artificial intelligence strategy.

The company, which models itself as China's full-stack AI provider spanning everything from data centers and software to end-user products, detailed its new Qwen Glasses N1 series at an event in Hangzhou. With prices starting at 2,999 yuan ($450) before discounts, they're no cheaper than industry leader Meta Platforms Inc.'s Ray-Ban smart glasses, showing Alibaba's effort to compete on quality and features rather than just price.

Mirroring Meta's strategy, Alibaba is endeavoring to turn smart glasses into an entry point for its AI tools and agents. Meta last month expanded its lineup of smart glasses with a simplified, camera-free model priced at $349, designed primarily for interaction with the new Muse AI assistant.

The new Alibaba glasses include improved 50-megapixel cameras and sensors, with a Pro edition priced at 3,499 yuan featuring new eye-tracking functions, said Wu Jianjun, general manager of Qwen AI hardware products. The new glasses will offer 25 hours of standby time or 9 hours of music playback from one charge, Alibaba said. Coming roughly a year after November's first edition, the new glasses more tightly integrate Alibaba's Qwen AI assistant and expand on its functionality.

Users will be able to speak to the AI agent via bone-conduction microphones, and the glasses also support shopping functions, payments and health tracking. Alibaba Chief Executive Officer Eddie Wu last month reiterated the company's ambition to develop all-stack AI, from large language models and chatbot apps to AI chips and hardware.

To provide a more affordable way to access Qwen, Alibaba also started sales of its new AI earbuds named Qwen Clip. These were jointly developed with headphone maker Bose Corp. and are priced at 1,299 yuan.

articles.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
articles.summary: The chatbot startup is looking to sell its assets to Disney after years of legal challenges and safety concerns.
articles.body: Character.AI, one of the first breakout startups of the generative AI boom, has filed for bankruptcy and is selling some of its assets to Disney. The company, which builds various online bots for users to chat or roleplay with, has faced mounting scrutiny and lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, but has continued releasing updates and products in recent months. In a press release and blog post published Monday, Character said it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US to facilitate the sale of the company and its assets. “Over the past year, we’ve taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve our business amid significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds,” the company said. In its bankruptcy filing, Character listed estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million. As part of the proposed sale, Disney would serve as the lead bidder for Character.AI’s assets, setting a baseline for competing offers. Disney would pay $20 million for certain undisclosed assets, and provide transition support “using former Company employees it has hired.” It would also receive a nonexclusive license to unspecified intellectual property. Disney’s involvement comes shortly after the entertainment behemoth hired Character.AI’s former CEO Karandeep Anand as chief technology officer, part of its growing push into AI. Anand’s tenure as Character CEO lasted just over a year and during that time he oversaw the company’s move into microdramas. Disney has previously complained that Character was damaging its brand and exploiting its intellectual property by allowing unauthorized chatbots of its characters, including sending cease and desist letters. Along with Anand, Disney also said it expected “a number of Character.AI’s technical team” to join the company. The move resembles a kind of “acquihire” strategy that has become increasingly common in Silicon Valley as a means of hoovering up startups’ talent that sometimes leaves the original company struggling to survive. Character.AI has survived it once already — Google spent over $2 billion to hire away much of the company’s talent, including co-founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, in 2024. Character said it expects the sale process to be completed by late November or early December and plans to continue operating its services, including paid subscriptions, in the meantime. However, the company warned that “the platform will be wound down” if a suitable bid does not emerge. “As we navigate this process, maintaining a safe and engaging experience for our community remains a top priority,” it said.

articles.title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
articles.summary: The startup will sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million.
articles.body:
Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document , the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.

“Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the board determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders,” Character.AI CEO Colin Adams said in a statement.

The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.

The company said Disney will provide transition services via former Character.AI employees who joined the entertainment giant last month alongside its former CEO Karandeep Singh Anand .

Adams said the company would continue operating during the sale process, which is expected to close in late November or early December. However, he did note that there isn’t yet a bid for the company’s assets or a buyer.

“We hope that the sale process will yield an actionable proposal that will allow continued operations of the Character.ai platform. If such a bid is unavailable, however, the platform will be wound down,” Adams wrote.

Character.AI has had a tumultuous five years. Founded by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper, and Daniel De Freitas in late 2021, the startup initially focused on training foundation models and developing an AI chatbot platform that lets people create custom characters they could chat with.

By September 2022, the startup reached unicorn valuation with a $150 million fundraise on the back of high demand for its platform, with the company saying at the time that its users had exchanged more than 2 billion messages with its bots in five months, and active users were averaging more than two hours on the platform daily.

In May 2023, the Character.AI’s apps attracted more than 1.7 million installs in their first week after launch. But about a year later, in August 2024, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license the startup’s models, and both Shazeer and De Freitas returned to the search giant . At that time, the startup’s general counsel, Dominic Perella, stepped in as interim CEO, and the company moved away from training foundation models to focus on growth.

Character.AI’s traction didn’t slow, however, with its platform recording 20 million monthly active users by October of that year.

But things got difficult after the startup was sued following the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot on its platform. Soon after, Texas launched an investigation to assess if the platform conformed to child privacy and safety laws. The company subsequently settled some of these lawsuits , added more safety features, and banned minors from its platform.

In June of last year, the company appointed Anand, a former Brex and Meta executive, as CEO, and expanded its products to add AI video generation, and social feeds. The company has since tried to introduce new ways to spur user engagement via interactive storytelling formats as well as microdramas.

But the fact that the company had to file for bankruptcy shows that such changes couldn’t move the needle on sustainability for the startup.

It also shows that consumer-facing AI products are really hard to scale and monetize. Character.AI was one of the top apps in terms of time spent, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. But high engagement can be a double-edged sword; AI costs rise the more people use the app, which consequently also increases the pressure to monetize users.

Character.AI has raised over $193 million in funding across multiple rounds from investors including Lightspeed, SV Angel, Greycroft, and a16z, according to PitchBook.

articles.title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases | TechCrunch
articles.summary: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.
articles.body:
Personal AI agents are increasingly making transactions on their users’ behalf, but given the nondeterministic nature of large language models, AI bots are prone to doing what they’re not supposed to. Which, in this case, raises the possibility of AI misfiring and making unauthorized transactions.

To get ahead of this problem, American Express is introducing a new framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction.

The idea is that there should be a way to ensure that the customer’s purchase instructions are carried throughout the transaction lifecycle, Amex says, from the purchase to everything that follows.

Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.

“These new transactions will have a consumer, a merchant, and an agent,” explained Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy, Hannah Bozian, in an interview with TechCrunch. She said the company wanted to ensure that agentic transactions are still “seamless, trusted, and secure, the way our card members expect them to be.”

This framework’s release follows the company’s April launch of Amex’s Agentic Commerce Experiences, or the ACE Developer Toolkit, which includes a handful of services that now include the intent framework.

Amex said it has not yet seen an increase in disputes because of agentic commerce, but it wanted to be proactive in building this technology as this type of commerce scales. In part, that’s because consumers have signaled they’re open to trying agentic commerce.

In a recent Amex Trendex report, 66% of surveyed U.S. consumers said they’re likely to use AI agents to research the best price for a product or service, and 61% said they’re likely to use it for a product or service recommendation over the next 12 months, the company told TechCrunch.

To start, Amex’s new intent framework begins with a Create Intent API, which will capture the customer’s purchase instructions along with other constraints they may have included in their request, like the merchant’s name, maximum budget, and other product preferences. How this intent is collected may vary depending on the AI model involved, but the plan is to make this framework flexible enough to support all agentic commerce models, Bozian said.

The customer then authenticates their identity and signs off on the intent captured by the agent.

Then an Intent ID, a unique identifier representing the intent, is created, along with a Proof of Intent Token, which includes the customer’s high-level constraints. This token is used to obtain a secure digital payment credential that the agent will use at checkout instead of the customer’s actual credit card number. In doing so, Amex says, the purchase will remain secure while being aligned with what the customer authorized the agent to do.

This Intent ID and token can also be used in different parts of the transaction process, helping companies to manage areas like fraud prevention and dispute resolution, Amex said.

“Our approach differs from the implementations of others in that it pulls intent earlier into the transaction flow. And this is important because it helps mitigate some risk before the risk occurs,” said Bozian. She offered the example of a customer asking an agent to buy white Nike sneakers in a size 9, but the agent submits a request to purchase shoes from Adidas. In such a case, Amex could prevent the transaction from going through because the agent made a mistake.

Bozian also notes that while many agents today ask for customer consent before making a purchase, Amex foresees a future where agents may act much more autonomously in some cases. For instance, a consumer might allow their agent to re-order household staples, like paper towels or toilet paper — categories in which the only real constraint is the price and size, not merchant or brand. In these scenarios, it makes sense to have technology in the loop performing that extra check, to ensure the transactions match the customer’s intent.

Having a log of what was authorized by which agent and when could also help address fraud on behalf of the agent, she noted.

Amex is already in discussions with partners across the payments ecosystem for implementing ACE, which includes the agentic tokens that contain Amex’s payment credentials, as well as other parts of the developer kit.

The company said it plans to actively develop ACE further as the agentic commerce ecosystem evolves.

On October 13 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ‘s Industry Stage, Amex VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy at American Express, Hannah Bozian, will discuss the company’s new “Intent Intelligence Framework” in more detail, and what it means for the world of agentic commerce.

articles.title: Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home
articles.summary: As Apple debuts Siri AI in the home, it’s focusing on a beautiful screen and hiding your text messages from your kids, rather than innovative smart home features.
articles.body: It’s finally here: Apple’s long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it’s gorgeous. The HomeView puts a small, vibrant screen atop a speaker base for taking video calls, beautifully displaying photos, and providing information at a glance with Apple’s Siri AI voice assistant. The device’s square shape makes it feel less imposing than larger smart displays like Google’s Nest Hub Max or Amazon’s Echo Show 11, and I can see it fitting nicely on my kitchen counter — though it might be a hair too big for my bedside table. The HomeView is the centerpiece of Apple’s new push into the home. It costs $299 and launches alongside a new collection of cameras, thermostats, and a door lock designed for Apple Home. As a smart home hub, Matter controller, and Thread Border Router, the HomeView can orchestrate these and other Apple Home and Matter smart home devices. It’s available in eight countries at launch: the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and India. Preorders are open now, with devices shipping November 13th. [Image: The HomeView can sit on a table or counter and display customizable widgets. The new smart display has Siri AI built in, enabling natural-language voice interactions to ask general knowledge questions, control smart home devices via voice and touch, and get information using personal context from your text messages, calendar, and emails. Personal context requires facial recognition and for your Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone to be on the same network, so your kids can’t peek at your texts over breakfast. The HomeView can display neatly formatted recipes for following along as you cook, keep you in the picture on FaceTime video calls with Center Stage, and show live feeds and footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. The HomeView’s 7-inch square screen sits atop a surprisingly small aluminum speaker base, attached by an adjustable stainless steel arm. It has no physical volume or power buttons, and no cover for the 12-megapixel FaceTime camera, which Apple says is used only for video calls and facial recognition. [Image: The many faces of HomeView. The screen offers a variety of customizable “faces” that feel more like a big Apple Watch than a small iPad. When idle, the HomeView can display photo faces, clock faces, and Snoopy faces, or you can use a modular face to show widgets from your most-used apps, such as your to-do list, world clock, and podcasts. A home widget face offers controls for lights, climate, cameras, and other devices. I haven’t had a chance to try the device yet, but I saw a demo showing how swiping up from the bottom of the screen pulls up a familiar app grid with Apple’s core apps — like Messages and Apple Music — all available. [Media: Apple also showed a video demoing how it envisions a family of five using the HomeView around the kitchen counter during the morning rush. From pulling up a French toast recipe for breakfast to checking the calendar for the day to receiving a FaceTime call to asking it to find lost keys, Apple pictures the HomeView stepping in to help with common minor household crises. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The video shows the daughter sending a text message to her secret boyfriend from the HomeView, and the younger brother being foiled from attempting to read it because it shuts off when it doesn’t see her face, and then everyone views a live feed of said boyfriend arriving at the front door. The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone. I’ve always seen smart displays as a good option for controlling smart home devices without having to pull out my phone and open an app. Apple’s vision for the HomeView takes that to its natural conclusion: you don’t have to pull out your phone for anything when you’re home since it’s all available on the HomeView (well, at least all of Apple’s apps). It’s an iPhone for your home. [Image: The HomeView can be wall-mounted, with the option of POE. The HomeView comes in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. It features two speaker drivers in the display, plus a woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators in the base for bass. Based on initial listening, the sound hits a few notches above the HomePod Mini but doesn’t compete with the HomePod. There’s a wall-mountable version without the speaker base that also costs $299 and comes with three mounting options: plug-in, in-wall power, and in-wall PoE. Apple says the audio is tuned for wall placement, but I didn’t get to hear it in action. The screen is wrapped in an aluminum case and has no physical buttons; the frame is just dotted with a speaker grille and microphone holes. It has a Liquid Retina display — that usually means LCD in Apple’s language, though the company didn’t clarify — with True Tone support and ambient light adjustment, and it can go up to a bright 500 nits and down to a super-low 0.3 nits, which Apple says makes it usable as a bedside clock. The screen is large enough to see clearly from across the room but doesn’t adjust as you approach. You tap widgets to access different apps and controls, or use voice to tell it what to do. [Image: [Image: While the HomeView functions as an Apple Home Hub — it enables local control of supported devices, creation of scenes and automations, and support for HomeKit Secure Video — the device feels less like a focused smart home controller and more like a way to use your iPhone less when you’re at home. The HomeView supports a number of Apple’s own apps, including Calendar, Reminders, Messages, and Music. Apple says it also works with third-party audio and video apps that support the CarPlay architecture. A few audio apps, such as Spotify and Audible, are available, but no video apps yet. [Image: You can pick up conversations started with Siri AI on the HomeView in the Siri AI app on the iPhone. And vice versa. Siri AI on HomeView is the same voice assistant as the upgraded version that arrived on the iPhone with iOS 27. It has no smart display-specific features or home-control features; it offers broad world knowledge, personal context, and natural language understanding. I saw a demo where it accepted chained requests and retained the context throughout, such as adding an event to the calendar, then setting a reminder for that same day, and adding an item to a grocery list. However, chained requests for home devices are limited to specific device types — you can turn on the lights in the living room and the bedroom, but you can’t lock the front door and adjust the thermostat with one command. Both the tabletop and wall-mounted devices have the same features; only the mount differs, but where you place them will likely dictate how you use them. A HomeView on the kitchen counter feels more tailored to content consumption, music, and cooking, while a wall-mounted version fits more of the smart home control center role. In its demo space, Apple mounted a HomeView near a front door with the smart home widget enabled, allowing touch control of locks, the thermostat, and lights. It can push a live feed from a doorbell camera when someone rings the bell and display up to nine live streams from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. When you tap on a widget, it becomes a full-screen controller. I saw the thermostat controls, and they were large and easy to use. I haven’t yet gotten to play with any other widgets or try controlling it with voice commands. [Image: HomeView supports up to six profiles and uses facial recognition to switch between them so only you see your personal information. The HomeView’s key software feature is intelligent switching that lets the screen move from a household device to a personal device. It uses facial recognition and the presence of your recently unlocked iPhone on the home Wi-Fi network to authenticate you. Once it knows who you are, it can show your customized HomeView layout and, if you have an AI-capable iPhone, use personal context to pull up that recipe Mom texted you or play that song your friend sent. Without recognizing the user, Siri AI on HomeView can show the live doorbell feed, answer general questions, control some smart devices, display recipes, and play audio and video. Apple allows the device to support up to six profiles, but each user must have an iPhone or iPad updated to the latest OS. Apple says the microphone and camera data used for profile recognition is processed on a Secure Exclave running on the device’s A18 chip, which Apple says it can’t access, the OS can’t access, and apps can’t access. [Image: You can hand off recipes from Safari on your iPhone to the HomeView, and it formats them for following along while cooking. My concern is how seamlessly it will switch between profiles and how limited it will be when it doesn’t recognize you — I’ve had too many instances of yelling at Siri on my HomePod because it refuses to find my iPhone until I authenticate on the iPhone I’m asking it to find. Some smart home controls, like viewing recorded footage or controlling security accessories, require an authenticated user, which I can see causing problems if it’s too slow or if you’re trying to get things done without standing in front of the device. Based on early impressions, and without yet getting my hands on the HomeView, I think success here hinges on how much people really want to use a communal device for personal interactions. The demos I saw were engaging and fun, and its deep integration with your iPhone gives it more to work with than a device like Amazon’s Echo Show, which has a similar profile feature but less personal information to offer. However, all the demos work just as well with Siri AI on your iPhone, and the whole system seems precariously tied to said phone. Beyond the personal context features, I didn’t see a compelling smart home use case that I haven’t seen on competitors’ smart displays. In classic Apple style, the HomeView looks gorgeous as well as intuitive to use, and if it can actually keep phones off the kitchen counter at meal times, that might just be its killer feature.

articles.title: Google finally releases Gemini 4 Argon
articles.summary: Google has been trailing its rivals for months, but says Argon can compete with top models like Anthropic’s Fable and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra.
articles.body: After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it can compete with the best the industry has to offer. Google says Argon delivers “frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows,” while cutting down on hedging, repetition, and the cliches that continue to plague AI chatbots. The company claims Argon outperforms rival models like GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 across a range of benchmarks, including coding, cybersecurity, science, finance, and law. Google says it’s already putting Argon to use internally, such as finding and patching cybersecurity vulnerabilities, halving the computing power needed to power YouTube’s comments section, and debugging the drone physics simulator for Alphabet’s drone delivery company Wing. The model is rolling out today to Google’s higher-tier Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI mode in Search, as well to Ultra subscribers on its agentic development platform Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Argon will be available to Plus subscribers or free users. Google is pricing Argon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable 5 models. Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period finishes — Argon will still be significantly cheaper than its frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs in practice, as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks. The launch fills in some of the blanks left behind from when Google first teased Argon a few weeks ago. In line with other recent frontier model releases, the public rollout follows a limited release to a select set of “trusted cyber defenders” to be tested for potential risks. Argon is Google’s first major frontier release since Gemini 3 in late 2025. In the intervening months, impressive models from Anthropic and OpenAI have seen Google trail far behind its rivals. Seismic internal shakeups raised further doubts about the company’s ability — or desire — to reclaim its position and compete at the frontier of AI. But Argon’s arrival suggests we can’t count Google out of the AI race just yet. Landing just a day after Meta announced its own frontier model, Muse Wonder Full, Argon is a reminder of how quickly the balance of power can shift in AI, and that the frontier is far from a two-horse race.

articles.title: Actress Mia Goth says it’s ‘incomprehensible’ that Instagram allowed an AI image of her to spread
articles.summary: A viral photo purporting to show Mia Goth in a T-shirt seemingly referencing her divorce spread from Instagram across the web. It was AI.﻿
articles.body: Earlier this month, news broke that actress Mia Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. An Instagram post from the account miagoth_ — marked with a blue verified checkmark — quickly spread. The post shows Goth in a T-shirt that reads “MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN” in bold black letters. The Beyoncé song “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)” had been added to the Instagram post. Hundreds of thousands of people — including some in the entertainment industry — liked the image, and entertainment outlets like OK! and even People wrote about it as if it were authentic. Soon, screenshots of the post were shared widely on other social media platforms. But the image, Goth’s representatives say, was AI-generated, posted by an account they had asked Instagram to remove. “Mia Goth does not have ownership of, nor does she engage in social media on any platform. We have filed multiple complaints with Instagram to remove the verified fan account which continues to post counterfeit, AI images of Mia Goth,” Christine Tripicchio, a representative for Goth, told The Verge in an email. “The fact that this fan account meets Instagram’s criteria to qualify for a ‘blue check’ is disconcerting on a fundamental level. Beyond that, it is incomprehensible that Instagram evidently prioritizes the dissemination of forged and manipulated images over the protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” [Image: An image of Goth shared to Instagram, which her representatives say is AI-generated. The miagoth_ account was labeled as fan-run, but the blue checkmark — which for years signaled an official, authentic entity — likely caused confusion for many in and out of the industry (the page had over a million followers). Meta began selling blue checkmarks several years ago as part of a new program, allowing accounts like the fan page to secure “verified” badges even if they weren’t run by the person being depicted in content. Meta spokesperson Alex Dziedzan told The Verge the miagoth_ account was removed for impersonating a public figure. Rather than ban AI-generated content of real people, Meta has taken the approach of labeling some content created with generative AI. Photorealistic AI videos of people, for example, may require an AI label — but Meta’s own rules include a carve-out that the label is not required for still images. AI-generated content featuring real people, including public figures, regularly racks up millions of views on Instagram, and Meta executives have signaled that AI-generated content will be a key part of how users engage on the company’s platforms going forward. Entertainers including musicians and actors have for years raised concerns about their likenesses being used to generate AI content. In 2024, Scarlett Johansson said that OpenAI had used a soundalike for the voice of ChatGPT even after she declined to work with the company on the project. That same year, Taylor Swift endorsed Kamala Harris for president, saying AI-generated images of her posted by Donald Trump made her realize she needed to “combat misinformation” around who she would be voting for. Update, October 13th: Added response from Meta.

articles.title: Facebook will let you customize your feed algorithm using AI
articles.summary: Meta is launching a “Your Algorithm” feature on Facebook that lets users select topics they want to see more or less of in their feed and Reels.
articles.body: Facebook’s new “Your Algorithm” feature will let you directly add and manage topics you want to see in your feed and Facebook Reels. Meta says your recommendations “respond right away” after you make updates using the new feature by hitting “interested” or “not interested” for different topics. Your Algorithm previously launched on Instagram earlier this year, and Meta also launched a similar “Dear Algo” feature on Threads. Facebook users will be able to access Your Algorithm or select “interested” or “not interested” from the three dots menu on individual posts. The “interested” and “not interested” buttons may also appear under posts, and Meta says it “may ask follow up questions for more detail on what you liked or disliked. You can easily tell us, in your own words, what you want to see more or less of, and your recommendations will update in real time.” The new feature is part of a set of “AI-powered” tools Meta says it’s using to customize what users see on Facebook. It also says it’s using LLMs more in its ranking systems: “LLMs can incorporate the interests, context, and intent behind natural language, unlocking an algorithm you can actually talk to. Tell it what you want more or less of, and your recommendations respond in real time, adapting within the same session to reflect what matters to you right now.”

articles.body:
Melania Trump’s annual artificial intelligence (AI) competition for students is getting rebranded with President Trump’s preferred name of super intelligence (SI).

The first lady appeared in a video to launch the 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge on Tuesday.

“The largest initiative in America’s education began with one bold idea,” Trump said, “prepare America’s next generation to lead the world in the most transformative technology of our time: super intelligence.”

“America’s next groundbreaking idea is already sitting in a classroom,” Trump said.

“We must give our children the knowledge, tools, and opportunities to bring those ideas to life,” she said in a statement announcing the second annual challenge.

As part of the effort, students are to complete projects that involve “the study, development, or use of an SI method or tool to address community challenges” while educators “will focus on creative approaches to teaching or using SI technologies in K-12 learning.”

Trump said that more than 20,000 students in kindergarten through 12 th grade and from across the country, participated in last year’s inaugural initiative , which was then-called the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge.

The president said last month that he aimed to officially rebrand AI as SI.

“The use of the word ‘artificial’ makes intelligence sound fake,” Donald Trump said in September, before signing an order that all official U.S. documents would use the SI term going forward.

In her announcement about this year’s challenge, Melania Trump said that all schools that participate in the initiative will have a chance to earn an official mark called the First Lady Seal of SI Readiness.

The seal, an announcement from the first lady’s press office said, “recognizes schools that are taking meaningful steps to prepare students and educators to understand, use, and responsibly engage with super intelligence.”

articles.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
articles.summary: Shopify will let customers shop its catalog via AI agents by connecting their Shop accounts. The agent can browse products and make purchases with the user’s approval.
articles.body: More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions. Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog. (The catalog consists of both items on and off Shopify storefronts.) In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration. To set up the feature, customers connect an agent with their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that consolidates orders, tracks packages, and recommends products. Like the Muse partnership, customers use the one-click Shop Pay feature to check out within the conversation with the agent. Orders placed through the agent are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify is marketing the feature as a “personal shopper” that humans can give rules to, like setting budget guardrails or only displaying products with fast shipping. Buyers must approve each purchase. E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds in the era of AI — it’s no coincidence that many demos of agentic tools end with a transaction, whether it’s buying clothing, booking a flight, or ordering takeout on a human’s behalf. The tech industry, including big commerce players like Google and Amazon, are investing in AI-driven shopping tools where the end goal is an “agent” purchasing things for a human user. It’s also the basis of an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies like Perplexity — and more recently, Meta’s Muse — over whether agents should be able to shop on a customer’s behalf.

articles.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
articles.body:
A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.

Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.

These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.

The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.

The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.

In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data.

Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations.

U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. But he did rule that Apple could access the interview materials, alongside private LINE messages (from a messaging app) between individuals named in the case, including OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng.

The judge also approved depositions for Liu and Peng, along with a third individual, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Yew Tan. All three are former Apple employees.

However, the judge denied Apple’s request to expedite its access to OpenAI’s research and development in specific areas, like metal finishes and power management. He also denied several of Apple’s broader discovery requests, like access to OpenAI’s hardware research or information about what its former employees created while working at OpenAI.

That denial isn’t final, though; the judge left the door open for Apple to narrow its requests and try again.

articles.title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly planting a bug in a conference room
articles.summary: OpenAI says an employee was arrested after it found a “sophisticated recording device” hidden in its office. The employee was identified as 35-year-old Abdulrahman Alfozan, according to The San Francisco Standard.
articles.body: An OpenAI engineer was arrested after the company said it discovered a “sophisticated recording device” hidden in one of its offices. The employee, 35-year-old Abdulrahman Alfozan, is charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, according to a report from The San Francisco Standard. OpenAI’s post about the incident says it used its AI models to “understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.” [Image: Images of the alleged recording device from the complaint. As reported by The San Francisco Standard, OpenAI found the device plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive conference room. The device was reportedly covered in toilet paper and installed on or around September 28th. OpenAI says it fired the employee and referred the incident to the FBI. According to the Standard, he was arrested Friday and has remained in custody since, appearing in federal court for the first time on Tuesday. > We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work. > At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated. > We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.

articles.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room | TechCrunch
articles.summary: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."
articles.body:
OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms.

The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device.

The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices.

“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X.

OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team.

Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office.

Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee.

It’s not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to “capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology.”

Neither Alfozan nor his attorney could be immediately reached for comment. He faces five years in prison if convicted.

When reached, a spokesperson for the FBI reiterated a statement made by Patel.

“Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities,” Patel said.
